main_text.p: tum appellat. Polybius alicubi συναγ-[?] χ̓όντες[?], eorum collegium congregatum, aut confessum συναρχίαν[?] videtur indigitare. Cum his igitur de negociis gravioribus in concilio agitandis praetor praeconsultabat, nec de iis, nisi in id pars major consentiret, licebat ad concilium referre. Qui si aut omnes, aut majore sui parte propositum probarent, legibusve aut foederibus congruum judicarent, petentibus concilium dabant, volentes cum concilio agere, introducebant, dicendi copiam faciebant: qui e concilio suadere aut difluadere cupiebant, voce praeconis id facere jubebant. Saepe praetor ipse, si ingenio & facundiae suae fideret, de re prolixe disse-rebat. Lex vero habebat, ut, qui sententias dixerant, eas brevi forma in scriptum relatas postridie rursum examinandas concilio proponerent: quo facto suffragiis res permittebatur. Non licebat autem ultra diem tertium actio-nem extendere: intra quem terminum nisi de decreto convenisset, concilium dimittebatur. page.notes: Greek words in the first lines (συναγ-, χ̓όντες, συναρχίαν) are uncertain and marked [?]. Left edge has faint marks that look like show-through or a previous leaf, not printed text, and were left out. The long s is printed as f in places (e.g. "suadere"), which was normalised to s. Text runs on across the bottom of the page into the catchword.
